article.name: BrainAPI

contact.note: Published in the official README for commercial licensing.

article.summary: BrainAPI is a Python service that turns ingested material into an event-centered knowledge graph and exposes graph, passage, and typed-fact retrieval. This review distinguishes README design descriptions and selected current code paths from unmeasured behavior.

who_what.text: The official repository describes BrainAPI as a knowledge graph backed memory service for agents and applications, implemented as a Python API/server with REST and MCP interfaces, worker processes, and an optional console. The README names Lumen Labs as the project organization; this review does not infer individual maintainer roles.

architecture.text: The README's ingestion design sends text through specialized Scout, Observations, Architect, and Janitor agents. It models actions as event hubs linked to actor, target, and context, preserving a graph path for multi-step retrieval. The repository separately supports passage and vector search; this is a documented product architecture description, not an end-to-end runtime confirmation.

The inspected intent-memory API has a typed IntentFact with stable fact ID, text, verification status, subject/predicate/object, valid and invalid times, supersession pointer, source fields, writer, retirement reason, and fact kind. Source passages are a separate retrieval lane. This layer is distinct from the README's graph-ingestion pipeline.

BrainAPI exposes a brain_id scope. Intent helpers resolve a supplied BrainPAT against that brain; the guard rejects a token scoped to a different brain. The helper also derives a writer label from a truncated SHA-256 token digest. This source slice does not establish organization-wide tenancy behavior beyond brain-level access.

behavior.text: Document ingestion is described as asynchronous: POST /ingest returns a task ID while worker agents extract entities, observations and graph relationships. The README describes a lightweight mode that skips some extraction and validation work. This review did not inspect every ingestion worker or validate those claims at runtime.

The inspected intent service can remember typed facts and associate source keys/passages. It parses subject-predicate-object claims, writes graph nodes/relationships, tracks source metadata and validity, and serializes conflicting writes per brain, subject and predicate using Redis when available plus an in-process lock fallback. The latest main commit also changes extraction to use the configured LLM with regex fallback, as visible in the reviewed head commit.

Correction is a versioning/retirement operation: the service records a replacement and closes eligible prior relationships with valid_to/invalid_at and superseded_by metadata. The current code avoids closing a later-dated fact when an older fact arrives. This changes stored relationship properties; the README's broad append-only statement therefore describes event history at a high level, not an absence of mutable lifecycle metadata.

The inspected fact actions include verify, reject, and reset. Verification and rejection require a principal and append state-transition history metadata. Rejection changes retrieval status; it is not evidence of physical erasure. I did not find a general destructive delete operation in the inspected intent models/service slices, and the README says graph events are retained rather than deleted.

Context retrieval combines passage channels and graph paths, with source code defining bounded candidate collectors, rank fusion, relevance filtering, and optional request-stage profiling. Intent recall separately collects keyword graph matches, vector seeds, neighboring graph relationships, and matching passages, then merges, temporal-filters, conflict-annotates and ranks facts. The current main commit updates intent recall/check to reuse hybrid retrieval rather than a fixed 2,000-fact scan.

Fact provenance can include source document, URL, source key, writer, verification state, verifier/source/note history, validity timestamps and supersession identifiers. Retrieval returns fact/source evidence fields; provenance establishes the recorded source path, not that the claim is true. The generic context route can also return source passages and graph triples.

metrics.evidence: Hybrid retrieval and unmatched-result fields are implemented in the inspected paths; no adjudicated query workload was run.
Temporal validity and supersession paths are visible in code; no corrected-value probes were executed.
Rejection/retirement paths were inspected, but no deletion leak workload or general hard-delete path was verified.
BrainPAT-to-brain authorization checks are source-visible; no cross-brain isolation probes were run.
Facts retain source metadata and context can return source passages/graph triples; evidence support precision was not measured.
The source defines stage timing and bounded query collectors; no runtime measurements or ingest-to-recall timing were collected.
The README describes pipeline modes and the repo has cost-related paths; this review did not establish measured tokens, costs, or storage efficiency.
The source exposes request stage spans, wall/CPU/IO timing, candidate counts and privacy-safe diagnostic logs; these are code observations, not runtime telemetry from this review.

limits.text: This is a bounded review of selected current README, intent-memory, verification, retrieval, authorization, validity and profiling sources. It did not inspect every storage adapter, ingest worker, route, plugin, or deployment configuration.

The README's claims about traceable graph paths, append-only history and retrieval targets are documentation statements. Source-visible fact retirement mutates relationship lifecycle metadata, while the selected slice does not establish physical deletion across passage stores, backups, or exports.

No service, model, or benchmark was executed. This review cannot establish retrieval quality, correction accuracy, deletion leakage, isolation under deployment, latency, cost, or production reliability.
